name: First post-launch patch
summary: Rockstar's first update since launch fixes crashes, stuck weather, autosaves and phone calls that never came.
body: Version 01.002.002 on PS5 (about 604 MB) and 1.0.2.2 on Xbox Series X|S (about 1.6 GB) went out in stages on November 23.

Fixed: crashes; weather that stopped changing for long stretches; autosaves; story and mission phone calls that failed to arrive; wanted levels that could not be lost; the gym deadlift bar; and partners not handing over bags to sell to fences.

name: $3.79 billion on day one
summary: Take-Two says the game took $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales, the biggest entertainment launch on record.
body: Take-Two's figure is its own estimate of worldwide retail sales up to the end of November 19.
It also said 32.5 million copies were sold before release, a pre-order record across every platform.

name: Biggest launch in PlayStation history
summary: Sony counts more than 39 million players on PS5 and 683 million hours played in the first days.
body: It also set a PlayStation record for the most people playing one game at the same time.

name: The Album: Deluxe Edition
summary: A longer edition of the soundtrack album is out on streaming services, with 23 more songs from the game.
body: The Deluxe Edition adds 23 bonus songs to the original 34, for 57 in all.
The vinyl and CD releases stay the original edition.

name: Metacritic user score falls to 5.6
summary: Players' scores on Metacritic sit far below the critics' 99, and some fans hit back by marking down other games.
body: By November 21 to 23 the PS5 version's user score was 5.6, against a critic score of 99.

Complaints named include the slow first chapter, the 30 fps target, bugs and the lack of a disc. Some fans then gave zero scores to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and other games at the top of the all-time list.

name: Unofficial PC port taken down
summary: Take-Two had an unofficial project that ran the Xbox version on PC removed from GitHub, with 3,007 copies of it.
body: The project went up on November 21. Take-Two's copyright notice, published November 24, had GitHub disable it and every copy made from it.
There is still no official PC version.

name: Xbox frame-rate trick
summary: Players found a way past the 30 fps cap on Xbox Series X, but it averages only about 36 fps and can speed up animations.
body: Switching the console's output between 60 Hz and 120 Hz and going back to the game through Quick Resume lifts the cap.
Digital Foundry measured about 36 to 37 fps on average. Some animations run too fast, as the game's speed seems tied to its frame rate.

name: The Vice City easter egg is solved
summary: Four days after launch, players solved a long puzzle built on GTA: Vice City's cheat codes.
body: It leads to a portal into an area drawn like a PS2-era game, where Kent Paul (Danny Dyer) waits.
The full steps are on the encyclopedia page for the easter egg.
